newsitem.title: UK: British Steel may cut jobs due to strong stg - FT.
newsitem.headline: British Steel may cut jobs due to strong stg - FT.

text.p: British Steel is planning to accelerate job cuts in response to the rise of the pound and to fears sterling could appreciate still further if Britain stays out of a European single currency, the Financial Times said on Tuesday.
The paper said British Steel chairman Sir Brian Moffat last month ordered senior managers to give top priority to cost cutting amid signs the pound looked likely to remain strong.
Sterling has appreciated by around 17 percent on a trade weighted basis since August.
The Financial Times said British Steel lost around 100 million pounds ($162.3 million) profit for every 10 pfennig rise in the pound.
British Steel has shed 500 to 1,000 posts a year in the 1990s and is proposing to cut well over 1,000 jobs this financial year.
It would continue to cut more than 1,000 jobs annually unless there was a dramatic reversal in the pound, the paper said.
"There is a new sense of urgency. Though it is early days to quantify the cuts we will see a real lift-off," the paper quoted John Bowden, head of media relations, as saying.
